I need to consider what the "X-Y Position Indicator for a Display System" refers to.

The X-Y Position Indicator for a Display System was the original formal name given to the computer mouse in Douglas Engelbart's 1970 patent. This device was invented to indicate positions on a display screen using X and Y coordinates.

Looking at the other agents' answers:
- Three agents said "Mouse" with high confidence (0.93-0.95)
- One agent said "Light pen" with confidence 0.96

A light pen is a different input device that directly touches the screen, while the mouse is an indirect pointing device that controls cursor position through X-Y movements on a surface. The formal patent name "X-Y Position Indicator for a Display System" specifically refers to what we now call the mouse.

The majority of agents are correct here.
